newsitem.title: USA: Calif. water agencies narrow electricity suppliers.
newsitem.headline: Calif. water agencies narrow electricity suppliers.

text.p: The Association of California Water Agencies (ACWA) has narrowed to five the list of electricity suppliers vying to serve 110 of its members following the state's deregulation of the market next January.

Suppliers on the short list include Edison International's Edison Source; Bonneville Power Administration/Tucson Electric Power /Power Exchange Corp; New Energy Ventures/Louisville Gas & Electric; Enron Power Marketing /Portland General Electric PGN. /Northern California Power Agency; and Electric Clearinghouse Inc.
The proposals bid power in the range of 1.45 cents to 1.64 cents per kilowatt-hour delivered to the California border, the agency said.
The bids were in response to a "request for proposals" issued in October 1996.
The finalists represent the best prices bid for electricity generation, the water agency association said.
Potential suppliers of metering and billing, nominations and scheduling, and ancillary services will be selected at later dates.
The ACWA formed a sub-agency in May 1996 to pool demand and combine the purchasing power for 110 water agencies.
Potential electricity demand for the the entire association membership is 1,000 megawatts (MW).
No estimate is available yet for the quantity of energy that would be needed if some water agencies become aggregators for their customers.
A final selection will be made by mid- to late March, with contracts expected to be executed by mid-1997 with service beginning in January 1998.
